why: The merge step of merge sort, done with pointers: repeatedly splice the smaller of the two current heads onto a growing tail. A dummy node removes the special case for the first node.
hints: At any moment the next node of the result is the smaller of the two current heads.
Create a dummy node and a tail pointer. While both lists are non-empty, link tail.next to the smaller head, advance that list and the tail.
When one list runs out, attach the rest of the other in one step. Return dummy.next. O(n + m) time, O(1) extra space.
pitfalls: Either or both lists may be empty.
Don't forget to attach the leftover list at the end.
Reuse the existing nodes; building new nodes works for the judge but misses the in-place point.
statement:
You are given the heads of two singly linked lists, listA and listB, each sorted in nondecreasing order. Splice their existing nodes into one sorted list and return its head. Keep duplicates. Either list may be empty.

Worked example. listA = 1 -> 2 -> 4, listB = 1 -> 3 -> 4.

  • Compare 1 and 1: take either (say A's 1). Result: 1.
  • Compare 2 and 1: take B's 1. Result: 1, 1.
  • Compare 2 and 3: take 2. Then 4 and 3: take 3. Then 4 and 4: take A's 4.
  • A is empty; attach the rest of B (4). Result: 1 -> 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 4.
